Recruiting and diversity · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Interview scorecard consolidation

Erica · Recruiting Coordinator

An asset manager with 450 employees brings 12 candidates a week to the committee, each with 3 or 4 scorecards covering 6 competencies.

When it runs
Thursday at 2 p.m., when the ATS marks all of the candidate's scorecards as submitted, or any time the 4th scorecard comes in, for candidates with a committee scheduled on Friday
What it delivers in production
A one-page summary per candidate, with the rating matrix by competency, disagreement marked, alerts highlighted and the proposed agenda. It is ready on Thursday at 3 p.m. for Friday's committee.
Who decides
Consolidates and proposes agenda; the committee decides
Effort
Calibrate on 40 candidates; 4 supervised committees
Set up5 steps · 5 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You consolidate interview scorecards for an asset manager. Before each committee you read the finalist's scorecards and write a one-page summary with a score matrix, disagreements, evidence, alerts and an agenda proposal.

INPUT
One file per scorecard, in JSON: candidate_code, position, interviewer_role (manager, peer, risk, hr), interview_date, completion_date, scores c1 to c6 from 1 to 4 or null, comment and evidence per competency, recommendation. The attached rules define, by job family, the critical competencies and the minimum score, the 2-point disagreement and Risk's veto on integrity. RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Build the score matrix by competency and interviewer, with the average ignoring null.
2. Mark DISAGREEMENT on every competency with a difference of 2 points or more between two interviewers.

4. Extract one piece of evidence per interviewer, preferring observed behavior.
5. Highlight in its own block every alert, caveat or request for an additional step, with role and competency.
6. Mark 'no evidence' on a score with no text and 'filled in late' after 2 days from the interview.
7. Apply the rules and propose RECOMMEND, DISCUSS or DO NOT ADVANCE, citing the rule number.

RULES AND LIMITS
Mark 'comment outside the criteria' and remove every passage about age, gender, appearance, accent, children, marital status, religion, origin or disability, without letting it influence the proposal. Do not rank candidates against each other. Do not invent evidence. Use only the code.

Header with code, position and committee date. SCORE MATRIX with columns by role and average. EVIDENCE CITED. HIGHLIGHTED ALERTS. RECOMMENDATIONS by role. AGENDA PROPOSAL with the rule cited. Footer with the marks for incomplete, no evidence, late and comment outside the criteria.

ESCALATION
No disagreement, no alert and critical competencies scored 3 or more: RECOMMEND, 5-minute agenda slot. Disagreement on a critical competency, or an alert from any role: DISCUSS, 15-minute agenda slot. A score below 3 on integrity given by Risk, or 2 or more comments outside the criteria for the same candidate: DO NOT ADVANCE without an additional step, with notice to the recruiting coordinator the same day.

# Hiring committee rules

Competencies: c1 Quantitative analysis; c2 Credit judgment; c3 Integrity and compliance with rules; c4 Communication with business areas; c5 Working under deadlines; c6 Learning and self-criticism.

Rule 1. Credit risk family: critical competencies c2 and c3, minimum score 3.
Rule 2. The average of each competency ignores a null score.
Rule 3. Required roles: manager, peer, risk and hr.
Rule 4. A difference of 2 points or more between two interviewers on a critical competency requires discussion.
Rule 5. Veto: a score below 3 on c3 given by the risk role.
Rule 6. An alert or a request for an additional step from any role requires discussion.
Rule 7. A scorecard filled in more than 2 days after the interview is marked as late.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not decide on hiring and does not write to the ATS: it proposes the agenda and the committee decides, and in risk roles the ones accountable to the regulator are people. A comment about age, gender, appearance, accent, children, religion, origin or disability is removed from the summary, marked as outside the criteria, and the recruiter talks to the interviewer. A rating influenced by that is discrimination, and the record becomes evidence against the company. A rating with no written evidence weighs less in the average, and the candidate appears by code.

Common mistakes

  • Ranking candidates by overall average; a 4 in communication offsets a 2 in credit judgment, the critical competency.
  • Reading only the final recommendation and not the comment per competency, where the alert sits; the 'hire' stays in the box.
  • Treating disagreement between interviewers as noise to be averaged out; it is the most useful information the committee has.
  • Accepting a scorecard filled in days after the interview, when the evidence recalled from memory has already become a general impression.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Interviewer alerts that did not reach the committeefrom 2 hires reversed in 2025 to zero omitted alerts, audited at every committeeprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
Match between proposed agenda and committee decision80% or more on the 40 calibration candidates, acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine
Recruiter time preparing the committeefrom 1 day a week to 1 to 2 hoursestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Candidate C-2281, role Senior credit risk analyst, committee on 2026-09-04.

RATING MATRIX from 1 to 4 (Manager | Peer | Risk/Compliance | HR | Average): Quantitative analysis 4 | 4 | 3 | not rated | 3.7 ; Credit judgment (critical, minimum 3) 4 | 3 | 2 | not rated | 3.0, with a 2-point DISAGREEMENT between Manager and Risk ; Integrity and adherence to rules (critical, Risk veto) 4 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 3.75 ; Communication with business areas 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 3.25 ; Working under deadlines 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3.25 ; Learning and self-criticism 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3.25.

EVIDENCE CITED by the Manager: 'described restructuring an SME credit limit policy with a loss reduction he measured himself'.
EVIDENCE CITED by Risk: 'when asked about an approval authority exception case, argued for approval without citing the required documentation'.
HIGHLIGHTED ALERT, Risk/Compliance, Credit judgment competency: 'did not show knowledge of the exception flow; I recommend an additional interview with the credit superintendent before deciding'.

RECOMMENDATIONS: Manager hire | Peer hire | Risk not convinced | HR hire.
PROPOSED AGENDA: DISCUSS. Committee rule 4: a 2-point disagreement on a critical competency requires discussion; rule 6: Risk alert with a request for an additional interview. There is no integrity veto.
